title: Find what every run shared
statement: When many runs agree on a limit, find what they all had in common before calling it a limit.
example: Retrained on the same data with only its learning rate corrected, one multiple-choice item type went from 76.7% to 93.3%.
detail: Across eleven training runs every useful variant landed between 76.7% and 85.0%, and the band was recorded as the model's ceiling (`icloud-work/auto-memory-backup/project_14b_saturation.md`). All of them had been trained with a learning rate set far too low (`icloud-work/auto-memory-backup/project_lr_was_too_low.md`), and the project's memory rules now list "All 11 experiments saw X, so X is a law." among the patterns to refuse until shared confounds are checked (`icloud-work/auto-memory-backup/MEMORY_GOVERNANCE.md`). Retrained on the same data with the rate corrected, two multiple-choice item types went from 80.0% to 90.0% and from 76.7% to 93.3% (`icloud-work/auto-memory-backup/project_v20a_lr1e4_result.md`).
against: The fix did not lift everything: "| apush/mcq_set | 50.0% (0.862) | 36.7% (0.699) | **−13.3pp** |" (`icloud-work/auto-memory-backup/project_v20a_lr1e4_result.md`, line 26). The band came from runs scored on 60 multiple-choice prompts and mostly trained on multiple-choice items only, while the corrected run was trained on all types. The list of runs at the wrong setting names ten, not eleven, and one of them used 1.5e-5 (`icloud-work/auto-memory-backup/project_lr_was_too_low.md`, lines 24 and 31).

evidence.quote: - **"All 11 experiments saw X, so X is a law."** → no. Check the shared confounds (e.g., wrong LR across all 11).
**v8/v18/v9/v11/v12/v13d/v14a/v15/v16b/v17 all used LR 2e-5.** All experiments tonight are confounded by this mistake.
The pattern band is tight: every "useful" variant lands in [76.7%, 85.0%] aggregate.
